title: 1Password Business to self-hosted Vaultwarden
summary: Vaultwarden is the cheapest thing on this site to run — and the one where we most strongly urge you to weigh the risk, not just the price.

you_lose: 1Password's security team, audits and bug-bounty programme
Travel Mode, Watchtower breach monitoring and account recovery
Someone else being responsible when the vault server goes down
you_gain: A Rust implementation light enough to run on the smallest box any provider sells
Bitwarden-compatible clients on every platform, so the apps are not the compromise
Free seats and free family sharing

caveats: A password vault is the single worst thing to lose. If you are not confident you will keep backups tested and the host patched, the honest answer is to stay on 1Password however the arithmetic reads.
Vaultwarden is an unofficial reimplementation of the Bitwarden server. It is well regarded and widely used, but it is not the vendor's own code.
Exposing it to the public internet needs a reverse proxy with TLS and, ideally, fail2ban. That is in the maintenance estimate, and it is not optional.
The maintenance estimate here is deliberately higher than the software needs, because security patching on this box is not something you get to defer.
